title: Cheese and onion rösti with mushrooms and eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, onion, cheddar, mushrooms, butter, eggs and oil are all ordinary kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, a tea towel and a frying pan, and squeezing and frying rösti is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 600g potato with an onion and 50g cheddar makes four decent cakes, squeezing them dry and frying them for 5 minutes a side will crisp them, and one egg each with 250g mushrooms suits four people.

honest_times.reason: The 20 cook minutes are not unattended because the rösti, then the mushrooms, then the eggs are all fried one after another at the stove, so it is about 35 minutes of hands-on work for a breakfast asked to be quick.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item is used: the oil is split as 2 tbsp plus the rest, thyme goes in with the mushrooms and 'season' covers salt and pepper, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot potato rösti breakfast suits a February morning, and the potatoes are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, like a neighbour explaining it.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potato, mushrooms and eggs make a filling, real-food breakfast with protein and vegetables that a family would happily eat again.
